frontier_modelled.token_basis: input = chat-mode prompt tokens counted by the local Qwen3.5 tokenizer (frontier tokenizers differ); output = local chat-mode answer length as a stand-in
frontier_modelled.cost_per_successful_outcome_note: Denominator is the number of tickets the LOCAL chat model got right (measured). This is not a frontier accuracy claim.

local_cost_modelled.method: wall time x public on-demand price of a comparable CPU instance (box compute itself is unbilled)

instance.name: AWS c7i.2xlarge (8 vCPU, 16 GiB), Linux on-demand

orion_review.rule: score_only or none = fails Orion's review. The score is a stop/route label and never counts as catching a false claim. No claim in any answer was verified by this harness.

assumptions.pnl_line: ASSUMPTION: model spend books to 'Cost of revenue: support inference'; tickets routed to a person book to 'Cost of revenue: support labor (human review)'. Not taken from any company's chart of accounts.
assumptions.moved_off_frontier: Reference scenario is an ungated harness that sends every ticket/step to a frontier chat model. moved_off_frontier=True when the gated harness stopped the item or routed it to small_model or human. Empty on rows that are not a routing/stop decision.
assumptions.cost_per_successful_outcome: Per row this repeats the mode-level figure: modelled local compute cost for that mode / tickets that mode classified correctly (measured). Empty on seeded rows (no gold outcome).
assumptions.threshold: 0.8: one untuned threshold for every gate, taken from the original pitch ('below 0.8, stop and flag a human'). Score = probability of the safe/chosen answer.
assumptions.person_facing: Bitext tickets are customer-facing, so triage gates run with person_facing=True: a low score routes to a human reviewer. There is no reject action in the code.

empty_columns_note: Columns are filled only where they apply (e.g. retry_loop_stopped only on retry-loop rows). A column listed here was empty on every row.
